scale: Proctor is permissioned and acts on a person's machine on their behalf, so the skill's scale puts it at A through J, plus K for a real window on a real display server and L for more than one process. All twelve are recorded below with their denominators.

writePosture.K_L: own instance: /Applications/Proctor.app pid 38168 and launchd agent app.fledgeling.procter.agent. TextEdit pid 51872 used as disposable AUT for overlay exclusion and guest refusal.
writePosture.B_E_F_H_J: this Mac, this session's own agent, and a disposable TextEdit document; no file the operator owns is written and the policy surface is only read
writePosture.C_D_G_I: Proctor drives its own status window on this Mac. The clipboard is read before the copy controls and written back afterwards; the agent restart is run last and waited for; no toggle is left changed.
writePosture.restored: the clipboard was put back, every switch was toggled back, and the settings file the sweep created was removed so all nine switches read builtInDefault again

forcedLive.how: SIGSTOP, so the socket is accepted and never answered
the window's own Restart agent control
one press on a consent-gated switch

notForcedLive.state: a required permission denied or unconfirmed
notForcedLive.why: forcing it means revoking the operator's own TCC grants, which is not this campaign's to do
notForcedLive.coveredInstead: StatusChecksTests, MenuBarIconTests and AgentRecoveryTests hold the decision over granted, denied and unconfirmed, which is where the rule lives; the render of that state is not asserted

A_stateMatrix.note: Recovery is asserted in each case: every forced state returned to ready in the same session.

C_interactionIntegrity.asserted: every enabled control was activated and its effect looked for in the window tree; a control whose effect is outside this window is named rather than counted as dead

restartControl.note: exercised last because it takes the agent down and brings it back

D_keyboardAndAccessibilityFloor.note: Tab is posted as a synthetic key and accepted. Full keyboard-only completion of the primary journey is not asserted here: the journey ends in System Settings, which is another application.

E_dataShapeStress.asserted: an odd predicate is either answered or refused by name, never a crash or a silent empty

rows.check: policy status is readable and reports its posture
the audit trail is signed and encrypted at rest
the guest gate is decided where the batch runs, not by the client that asked
rows.detail: PROCTOR_GUEST set on the shim did not refuse the batch. The shim carries no guest state; the agent reads it where the steps are performed, which is why CASE-0021 arms this by setting it on the agent instead.

G_twoSessionsAtOnce.asserted: two MCP clients on one agent both get an answer, and the queue reports itself
G_twoSessionsAtOnce.note: Not multi-user: one Mac, one person, one agent. Two concurrent sessions is the real shape of this sweep here, and the queue is what arbitrates them.

H_refusalHonesty.asserted: a refusal reaches the caller as a code with a sentence and a remedy, and never as a success

a targeting frame is no larger than a verify frame of the same window

halfOpen.forcedBy: SIGSTOP on the agent, so the listener stays bound and the reply never comes
halfOpen.before: client blocked past 25s and was killed by the harness; the window showed Ready throughout
halfOpen.after: window reads Agent down and "did not answer within 5s" at t+7.12s; SIGCONT restores Ready

privilegeSeparation.forcedBy: a core-profile shim naming proctor_guest and proctor_policy, which core does not advertise
privilegeSeparation.observed: both executed. tools/list returns 10 names on core and 21 on full, and tools/call accepts any real tool whatever the profile
privilegeSeparation.contract: MCPServer.swift:123 states it: the profile trims discovery so a host is not handed the whole catalogue as noise, and never blocks a host that widens its own surface
privilegeSeparation.reading: the profile is a token-cost trim, not a privilege boundary between principals, and the client choosing --profile core is the same principal that could name the tool. Recorded as the documented contract rather than a defect; the campaign record that claimed a refusal was wrong and is DEF-004

startupOrder.note: UI remained with Status window while agent was down; MCP tools failed immediately with agentUnavailable rather than spinning. First-run path was not re-executed (walkthroughCompleted=1 after Skip setup).

asFirstMeasured.note: proctor_find on the walkthrough/status tree: 8 AXCheckBox with empty title/label, 7 AXButton titled Details.

accessibilityFloorDetail.note: Recorded on 2026-08-19 as a note and left there, which is how a real accessibility defect survived two rounds of this campaign. It is DEF-007 now.

overlayRasterChannels.question: can any capture channel photograph a window whose sharingType is .none

channelsTried.result: no frame for the HUD; SCFrameStatus complete of fully transparent frames for the takeover panels
exit 1, "could not create image from window"

channelsTried.channel: screencapture -R over the rect the HUD occupies
channelsTried.result: shows whatever is behind the panel; the HUD is absent from the frame
obsoleted in macOS 15 and refuse to compile on this toolchain

overlayRasterChannels.conclusion: no channel on this lane can produce overlay pixels, and the agent capturing its own window does not change it. CASE-0008 and CASE-0010 stay n/a on a structural ground rather than an unattempted one

detectorDefectsFoundAndFixed: the scaling predicate counted a scrolled control as a clipped one and flagged 12 at every scale including the unchanged baseline
the arming harness passed suite display names to swift test --filter, matched zero tests, and printed "Test run with 0 tests passed", which reads as a clean sweep
this sweep runner wrote its transcript over its own call results, so a window handle came back empty and every window-dependent check silently measured a "requires window" refusal instead
the refusal predicate read only the top level of a response, so proctor_act batches, which report per step, looked like silent failures

totals.note: One failure, and it is L's half-open cell: the wedged agent that the status window went on reporting as Ready. It is DEF-002, fixed and re-measured in the same run. The other defects these sweeps found are DEF-001 reopen, DEF-005 the unexcluded pointer and DEF-007 the unnamed controls, each fixed and re-measured, which is why the rest read zero. A zero over 12 sweeps is only worth reading beside that list.
